text:
maria: FYI after rolling the CNI upgrade to the west2 GPU cluster (agents pool) we're seeing elevated east-west packet drops between worker pods, started ~10:30 UTC. Training jobs show retries and some RDMA resets. 😬

jon: saw that too. Iperf between pods in same node is fine, cross-node shows spikes and packet loss. numbers: 1-4% loss on short runs, baseline was ~0.0-0.2%.

kevin: any MTU changes during the upgrade? tunnels + encapsulation often break jumbo frames.

maria: we didn't touch host MTU. CNI changed default tunnel mode -> geneve and enabled hardware offloads toggle. I have kube-proxy logs and dmesg from one affected node.

infra-bot: deploy bot: cilium-upgrade-job finished for west2-gpu at 1851232000 by deploy/infra-pipeline.

jon: pasting quick outputs from a failing pod pair:

maria: ```
# from pod-a -> pod-b (cross-node)
$ ping -c 20 pod-b
--- ping statistics ---
20 packets transmitted, 19 received, 5% packet loss, time 19044ms

# dmesg snippet (worker-12)
[123456.789] cilium: dropping 1500B packet due to MTU mismatch
[123460.001] mlx5_core 0000:01:00.0: mlx5_core: QP 12345 error: RNR retry count exceeded
```

kevin: that mlx5 QP error smells like RDMA QPs affected by encapsulation path. If geneve reduced effective MTU on the overlay interface, large RDMA CMA setups will break.

alex: can we run `ip link` and `ethtool -k` inside host and compare veth/geneve mtu/tx offloads? I'll grab outputs.

maria: here's trimmed ip link from host (worker-12):
```
3: eth0: mtu 9000 state UP
68: genev0: mtu 1450 state UP
69: cilium_host: mtu 1450 state UP
```

maria: and ethtool offloads: genev0 GRO: off, GSO: on, TSO: on — but the CNI toggled some offload settings.

jon: ahh genev0 mtu 1450 vs host 9000 -> fragmentation happens at host where RDMA expects jumbo. That explains QP errors.

kevin: quick mitigation: roll back to previous CNI daemonset that had tunnel mode disabled (or set mtu to 9000 on encap) and re-enable host jumbo frames on overlay. Can we patch Cilium ConfigMap to set tunnel mtu to 9000 and disable offload changes?

maria: attempting a safe patch now: `kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap cilium-config --patch '{"data": {"tunnelMTU":"9000","enable-tunnel-offloads":"false"}}'`

alex: also recommend setting `disable-kernel-drop=true` for RDMA path in cilium (if available) — but test on canary first.

maria: canary applied to node-pool-gpu-canary. Running iperf between pods there: cross-node loss ~0.1% now. Looks promising.

jon: good. We should capture perf traces and packet captures to confirm reassembly. Can someone run tcpdump on genev0 and on eth0 during a failing job?

kevin: I'll schedule a controlled job to reproduce and collect tcpdump + `rdma link` logs. Leaving it to after-hours to avoid customer jobs.

maria: note: some pods rely on direct RDMA (ibverbs) so fallback to TCP slows training heavily. We need a post-mortem and a remediation checklist:
- verify overlay mtu matches host for RDMA workloads
- don't flip offloads in patch releases without compatibility checks
- add e2e test for large MTU and RDMA QP stability on canary pools

jon: +1. Also suggest adding a probe in Optimize that flags when encapsulation MTU < host MTU for clusters with RDMA-labeled nodes.

infra-bot: incident tracker created: INC-2026-045, priority P2. Assigned: eng-infra oncall.

maria: rolling the patch to remaining GPU nodes now, will monitor RDMA QP errors and packet loss for 2 hours before full rollout. Will update thread. :thumbsup:

alex: if rollback isn't possible, we can temporarily cordon gpu nodes and failover jobs to dedicated-non-rdma pool until fix.

kevin: capturing logs and pcap artifacts to s3://redwood-ops/incident/INC-2026-045/pcaps/1851234567/

maria: update: after patch rollout loss dropped to 0.2% cluster-wide and QP errors stopped on tested nodes. Continuing rollout.

jon: great work. Postmortem requested after stable window. Include config diffs and canary test outputs.

maria: noted. Closing canary in ~3h if stable. Thanks everyone.
